NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
2343-49 N. DAMEN AVENUE, CHICAGO

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated within 300’ from the Fullerton
Bus Corridor. The subject property is a unique irregular lot, currently improved with an industrial
building, The Applicant is planning to demolish the existing building and redevelop this property
with a new 4-story (with basement) residential building with 27 dwelling units and 16-car garage;
with roof top decks to be located on the principal building and on the garage. The Applicant needs
a zoning change from the existing M3-3 to a B2-3 zoning district to allow residential use at the
property and to comply with the bulk requirements of the Ordinance. The Applicant will also
need relief for variations to reduce the rear setback from 30’ required to 20’-10” proposed; to
reduce the loading berth from one to zero, to increase the height of the building from 55’ to 56’-
10” proposed (for the rooftop features); and to allow increased parking ratio from 13 spaces
required to 16 proposed.

Project Zoning Change from the M3-3 Heavy Industry District to a B2-3
Description: Neighborhood Mixed-Use District,

Use: Residential Building with 27 dwelling units

Lot Area: 11,661 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 2.9

Floor Area: 33,795 SF (see plans attached)

Density: 431 Square Feet per DU

Off- Street Parking: | Parking spaces: 16 (see Adjustment request below)

Setbacks: Front: 0°
Side: 0’ on each side
Rear: 20’-10” (see Variation request below)

Building Height: | 56’-10” per the attached plans (TSL bonus and request for variation
below)


1 The applicant will comply with Section 17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served
Locations, should such provisions be determined as applicable:

17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations. In B and C districts, any new construction
within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all of the following
specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B Transit-Served
Locations: while the subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is located within the
required distance from the Fullerton Bus Corridor, the subject property is not located within the
required distance of any CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit; consequently Section 17-3-
0308 is not applicable to this project.

2. The project also substantially complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-4-0504,
except paragraph E and paragraph C, since the proposed land use is designated in a non-
commercial use group, and the project is not located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail
street:

(a) The entire building fagade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.

(b) The requirements of Section 17-4-0504-C Transparency standards do not apply to the subject
development as proposed building is entirely residential (non-commercial use group) and there is
no commercial space which would require clear, non-reflective windows, and the project will not
provide any product display windows.

(c) The building will have a primary entrance door facing Lister Avenue.

(d) All off-street parking spaces will be located inside the principal building and will not be
visible from the right-of-way.

(e) The parking area will be located inside the building: in the basement and on the ground floor;
vehicle access to the parking area will come via the two proposed driveways, per site plan
attached.

3. The project is not required to comply with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly
Development Guide, the Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or
guidelines adopted by the Chicago Plan Commission.

With this proposed redevelopment the Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is in excess of
50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-
0208, therefore, in case this Section applies, the Applicant is requesting an Administrative
Adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE.

4. The project is not required to comply with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules
of the Chicago Department of Transportation. This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

118 Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) The Applicant seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from the rear setback
requirements of Section 17-3-0405-A, which states that for floors containing dwelling units,
the minimum rear setback is 30 feet. To mitigate site planning hardships on this substandard
and irregular lot, the Applicant requests a reduction in the required rear setback from 30 feet
required to 20’-10” proposed.

(B) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under Section 17-13-1101-D, from the loading
requirements of Section 17-10-1101, to reduce the required number of loading berth from
one to zero.

(C) The Applicant seeks relief for administrative adjustment under Section under the provisions
of Section 17-13-1003-EE from the parking regulations of Section 17-4-0301 Specific
Criteria for Transit-Served Locations, to increase the parking ratio, from 13 spaces required
to 16 spaces proposed.

(D) Section 17-3-0408-B Building Height Increase for Transit-Served Locations states that all
projects in B dash 3 subject to Sec. 2-45-115 that (a) qualify for and are granted a building
height increase under Sec. 17-3-0408-B.1 and (b) provide at least 50% of the required
affordable units on-site, are eligible for additional increases in maximum building height.
Since the subject property is a Transit Served Location and the project will provide at least
50% of the required affordable units on-site, the project is eligible for the building height
increase to 55 feet. In addition, to accommodate the roof top stairs enclosures and the
elevator enclosure, in case such rooftop features are deemed non-compliant with Section 17-
17-0311-C, the Applicant also seeks relief for administrative adjustment from Sec. 17-3-
0408-B, under Sec. 17-13-1003-L to increase the maximum Building Height from 55 feet
required to 56’-10” proposed.

(E) The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for
the proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the applicable provisions of the Zoning Ordinance would create
practical difficulties and particular hardships since the irregular configuration of the subject
property creates site-planning constraints that unnecessarily limit the reasonable development
of the property. The property has an irregular shape, with frontage on two public rights-of-
way, but a highly variable depth ranging from approximately 45.57 feet to 170 feet. These
conditions substantially constrain the ability to configure a new residential building while
simultaneously complying with the applicable rear setback, loading, parking, and building-
height requirements. The requested relief is narrowly tailored to address these site-specific
conditions and to permit a reasonable and functional redevelopment of the property. The
proposed development will provide 16 on-site parking spaces, private usable open space, and
modern floor plans for the dwelling units.

2. The requested relief is consistent with the purpose and intent of the Zoning Ordinance and
will facilitate an appropriate redevelopment of the subject property. The proposed
development is compatible with the established land-use pattern of the surrounding
neighborhood, which includes multi-story and multi-unit residential buildings. The project
will replace the existing obsolete industrial building with new residential housing and will
introduce additional dwelling units in an established, transit-served neighborhood. The
proposed development will make efficient use of an existing urban lot and infrastructure while
increasing the variety and availability of housing within the neighborhood.

3. Evidence of Practical Difficulties or Particular Hardship is as follows:

- The property in question cannot yield a reasonable return if permitted to be used only
in accordance with the strict standards of this Zoning Ordinance.

- The irregular lot configuration, variable and substandard depth, dual street frontage,
significantly limit the available building envelope. Strict application of all applicable
